title: Multi-region steering policies: latency-based routing, geo-pinning, capacity-aware steering
creator: Ava Ramaswamy
description:
Background: We need a unified, production-safe multi-region request steering layer to satisfy global SLOs and graceful degradation strategies. Current behavior is static region preference per org and naive fallback to next region on error. This ticket designs and implements three complementary policies: 1) latency-based routing (steer to region with lowest p95 latency for the API key/route), 2) geo-pinning (pin sessions to a preferred region for locality/consent reasons with TTL and sticky heuristics), and 3) capacity-aware steering (avoid directing traffic to regions approaching compute/capacity thresholds by using capacity signals from Dedicated control plane and host metrics).

Goals: - Reduce cross-region tail latency and p95 for interactive workloads by steering to low-latency regions. - Respect geo-pinning constraints for customers with data locality or compliance needs. - Prevent cascading overload by steering away from overloaded regions and enabling load-shedding where appropriate. - Integrate with existing circuit-breaker and fallback mechanisms so rollbacks are deterministic. - Provide observability and controls in Console: per-route routing policy, simulation mode, and canary rollout.

Design proposal (high-level): - Policy evaluation order: 1) Geo-pinning rules (hard constraints) 2) Capacity-aware gating (soft constraints with weight adjustments) 3) Latency scoring (dynamic score combining measured p50/p95 and historical token cost) -> final weighted selection. - Latency measurements: use client-observed RTT sampled at the edge plus server-side processing p95. Maintain a sliding window (5m, 1m, 30s buckets) per region per route. - Capacity signals: integration with Dedicated telemetry (queue length, GPU utilization percentile, free slots). Expose three capacity states: NORMAL, CONSTRAINED, UNAVAILABLE. - Circuit breakers: when a region flips to UNAVAILABLE, trigger immediate circuit and reroute; when CONSTRAINED, reduce traffic fraction and prefer lower-cost region. - Load-shedding: provide graceful shedding by rejecting non-critical requests (batch/low-priority) and offering configurable fallbacks (degraded model, longer response allowed) before returning 5xx. - Sticky session TTLs: geo-pinning uses session affinity cookie or token mapping with TTL default 6 hours, configurable per-customer. - Simulation & dry-run: routing policies can be simulated in Console (traffic shadowing) to measure expected SLO impact. - Config surface: per-API-key and per-route policy config (priority order, weights, thresholds) via Console and API; default global policy applied for new accounts.

Acceptance criteria: - New routing layer can be enabled per-route with rollout flag. - Latency-based routing lowers observed p95 by at least 15% for sample interactive workloads in our benchmark region set during a controlled canary. - Capacity-aware steering reduces error budget burn during a simulated regional capacity constraint by at least 60% vs baseline. - Geo-pinning honors "data residency" label for customers and never routes outside allowed regions. - Console shows per-region routing decisions and exposes a simulate toggle. - End-to-end tests for policy precedence, circuit breaker triggers, and load-shedding behavior.

Implementation plan (phases): - Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype latency scoring and per-route selection logic in the routing service; gather sample metrics from the edge. - Phase 2 (integration, 2 weeks): wire capacity signals from Dedicated telemetry, implement capacity state machine and circuit-breaker hooks. - Phase 3 (policy engine, 2 weeks): add geo-pinning store (consistent map + TTL), policy config API, and evaluation precedence. - Phase 4 (observability + console, 2 weeks): add dashboards, traces, and a Console simulate mode. - Phase 5 (canary + rollout, 1 week): canary in low-risk account set, expand based on metrics. Total estimate: 8 points.

Trade-offs & open questions: - Where to compute scoring? Edge (lower latency but more complex) vs centralized routing-service (easier to manage). Proposed: scoring at edge proxies for freshness with fallback to routing-service config. - Consistency of pinning vs ephemeral scaling: pinning map must be resilient to loss and have fallback to heuristic (IP affinity) on restore. - Privacy/compliance: geo-pinning must be auditable and restricted by org-level policy; security review required.

Testing & observability checklist: - Synthetic load tests that vary regional latency and capacity to confirm reroute behavior. - SLO dashboards: p50/p95/p99 per region per route, error rates, re-routed fraction, rejected (shed) requests count, circuit-breaker transitions. - Canary metrics: compare canary vs control on latency, errors, and cost. - Incubate a debug endpoint that emits why the routing decision was made (policy reasons) for support/debugging.

Migration & rollback: - Default policy remains current behavior until route-level flag enables new engine. - Rollout incremental: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% per account segments. - Fast rollback by toggling policy flag and allowing traffic to drain for pinned sessions.

Docs & links: - RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Multi-Region+Routing+RFC (draft) - Spike notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-routing-spike - PR TODOs: github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pulls/xxxxx (will be created) - Alert runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Runbook+Regional+Routing
comments: 2026-03-02 - Spike complete. Collected edge RTT samples for regions us-west1/us-east1/eu-west1. Initial scoring prototype reduced p95 in local test by ~12%.
2026-03-04 - Design review with PM and Console: agreed on simulate mode and per-route flags. PM requested exposed metric: re-route delta by cost bucket.
2026-03-06 - Security flagged geo-pinning audit requirement. Filed follow-up with security team to define retention and KMS access controls (SEC-2431).

2026-03-09 - Integrated capacity signal proto from Dedicated telemetry (ENG-8902). Observed momentary CONSTRAINED states during burst simulation; capacity-aware gating prevented full-region failover in test.
2026-03-12 - Implementation started: routing-service branch opened, unit tests for precedence logic added. Next: implement sticky session store with fallback heuristics.
